source.title: Detection Accuracy for Evaluating Compositional Explanations of Units
source.authors: Sayo M. Makinwa; Biagio La Rosa; R. Capobianco

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a different explanation-evaluation procedure can reveal specialized units, reporting a manual inspection of explanations from a vision model. It does not test the language-model audit or most other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the study's own analysis of units identified by its Detection-Accuracy stopping procedure. Its other reported comparisons of IoU, Detection Accuracy, and correlations with model prediction accuracy evaluate metrics, but do not directly measure the claim versions about language-model neuron jobs or out-of-sample explanation accuracy.
record.test_reason: This is a metric paper. It proposes Detection Accuracy for scoring concept explanations of final-layer CNN units and reports how the metric performs: IoU versus DetAcc comparisons, correlations with model accuracy, and DetAcc as a search stopping rule. It takes from prior work that units detect human concepts and never measures what share of units are interpretable. It does not compare interpretable shares across tools or architectures, and it does not test explanations' predictive accuracy on held-out data. The 179/245 count is a breakdown of its own method's length-1 outputs, not an interpretability share, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim that Detection Accuracy evaluates explanations more objectively than IoU. They report that it correlates better with model prediction accuracy (Tables 2 and 4). They say that, used as a stopping criterion, it gives explanations that better reflect what units learn and exposes new specialized units. They conclude it works better as an evaluation metric than as a way to select explanations.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses visual CNN units, ADE20K concept masks, and compositional explanations evaluated with Detection Accuracy; it does not use the language-model audit procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differing outcomes for Detection Accuracy used to select explanations from the beam versus used only as a stopping criterion; the specialized-unit result is from the latter setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Under IoU, length-3 compositional explanations beat single-concept Network Dissection explanations for nearly 100% of final-layer units in four CNNs. Under Detection Accuracy, single-concept explanations win for about 38–56% of units (Table 1). IoU rises with explanation length while DetAcc falls (Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How well a unit appears to be explained, and which explanation looks best, depends on the scoring metric; overlap metrics reward longer explanations.

fits_no_version.finding: Units whose DetAcc-stopped explanations are longer than length 1 are described as lexically coherent or incoherent abstractions, or as polysemantic. No count is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some final-layer CNN units remain polysemantic under compositional concept explanations.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference of the Italian Association for Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The specialized-unit classification relies on manual inspection. No held-out evaluation set for this analysis is reported in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–3 report metric comparisons and correlations with model prediction accuracy. They were left out because those outcomes do not directly measure the claim's unit-interpretability share or the listed explanation-failure tests.

untested.parts: All: no language models and no pole audit.
All: no language models, no scale comparison, no mixture-of-experts models.
All: no InceptionV1, no cat-and-car neuron, no test of pose or superposition.
All: no interpretable-unit share is reported, and no comparison across tools, architectures or regularization. The four CNNs appear only in the metric comparison (Table 1).
All: no attribution graphs or circuits.
All: no held-out test of whether explanations predict where units fire.
All: no activation simulation and no share of well-scored neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. The 179 count comes from manual inspection of the study's own method output, with no comparison of interpretable shares across tools, so it cannot show the share rising. The units studied are final-layer units of ResNet-18, AlexNet, DenseNet-161 and ResNet-50 trained on Places365 and probed with ADE20K. The specialized-unit analysis covers only ResNet-18.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole audit and its reported shares.
Language models, model scale, dense versus mixture-of-experts architectures, and trillion-parameter models.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car examples, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.

The study reports a result for a Detection-Accuracy-based explanation procedure on ResNet-18, but does not compare interpretability shares across architectures or regularization choices, test InceptionV1-sized models, or assess the essay's estimates.
Attribution graphs and whether they reconstruct behavior without replacement models.
The study does not test explanations on activations withheld from explanation generation or measure whether explanations predict firing on new examples.
The study does not score language-model neuron explanations on new text or report the share of neurons receiving good scores.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Manually inspected length-1 explanations produced when Detection Accuracy was used only as the compositional-search stopping criterion.

conditions.value: Detection Accuracy used only as stopping criterion

rows.measure: Number of length-1 explanations judged to be perceptual abstractions of their longer regular-compositional explanations
rows.value: 179 of the 245 units with length-1 explanations (∼73%)
rows.note: The authors say this procedure exposes a new set of specialized units. They also report that 245 of 512 units had length-1 explanations; the 179 count is based on manual inspection.
rows.check: This row counts outputs of the study's own search variant: units whose length-1 DetAcc explanation abstracts their longer explanation. It is not the share of interpretable units, and it is not compared against weaker tools or other architectures. It cannot bear on V4's claim that the interpretable share rises with better tools.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Manually inspected the remaining length-1 explanations produced when Detection Accuracy was used only as the compositional-search stopping criterion.

conditions.value: Detection Accuracy used only as stopping criterion

rows.measure: Number of length-1 explanations not in the identified perceptual-abstraction category
rows.value: 66 of the 245 units with length-1 explanations (∼27%); longer explanations failed to improve Detection Accuracy during the search
rows.note: This result describes exceptions among short explanations; it does not establish that those units are uninterpretable.
rows.check: This row is the complement of R1 within the study's own method output. It says nothing about interpretability shares or how they change with tools or architecture.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
